protocols.name: 0x (Matcha)
protocols.notes: Matcha is built on the 0x API. In the Swap API AllowanceHolder flow the user approves AllowanceHolder and calls AllowanceHolder.exec, which forwards to the current 0x Settler. Settler contracts are redeployed often, so their addresses rotate; 0x says never to hardcode them and to look up the current one on the deployer/registry 0x00000000000004533Fe15556B1E086BB1A72cEae with ownerOf(featureId) (2 taker-submitted, 3 metatransaction, 4 intents, 5 bridge). In the Permit2 flow the user signs a Permit2 EIP-712 message and sends the transaction straight to the current Settler, which is why no Settler address is listed. The legacy v1 Exchange Proxy is superseded by Settler and not listed.

protocols.name: CoW Protocol (CoW Swap)
protocols.notes: Most CoW Swap orders are EIP-712 messages signed off-chain against the GPv2Settlement domain and settled by solvers; users approve tokens to GPv2VaultRelayer (0xC92E8bdf79f0507f65a392b0ab4667716BFE0110), which they never call. The transactions users do send are ETH Flow orders (native ETH) and pre-signatures or cancellations on GPv2Settlement. Both contracts are deployed on OP Mainnet too, but the CoW SDK lists OP Mainnet only as a bridge destination, not a chain CoW Protocol trades on, so it is not listed. UniswapX (not listed) works like this as well: users sign EIP-712 orders and fillers call the reactors, so users do not send transactions to them.
